title: Per-request lightweight telemetry anchor: low-overhead span attach for async flows
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: SDKs and middleware occasionally lose trace/span fidelity on long-lived or batched async requests (streaming responses, background workers and scheduled retries). Existing instrumentations either add measurable latency (synchronous context lookups, heavy TLS metadata copies) or require users to adopt opinionated frameworks. Goal: implement a per-request "telemetry anchor" concept in our language SDKs that provides a tiny, application-visible tokenic anchor attached to request metadata and a non-blocking, low-overhead span attach/detach path for server and client SDKs. The anchor should enable precise span attribution across async boundaries (timers, promise chains, worker pools) with a fallback no-op path when not enabled to keep overhead near zero for cold paths.
acceptance_criteria: NodeJS SDK: anchor attach/detach API that is O(1) and measured < 6us median per attach on 2.5GHz core with no-op mode
Python SDK: context manager + async contextvar integration preserving span id across await boundaries and background tasks
Instrumented server/startup: add anchor header propagation over HTTP/gRPC and websocket handshakes without breaking existing trace header formats
End-to-end test: streaming upload + server worker offload preserves single logical span with correct start/end timestamps and parent id
Fallback: if anchor header missing, instrumentation is a no-op and sampling decision preserved
Documentation: API surface documented in SDK reference and a migration guide for customers running custom instrumentations
implementation_notes: Design anchor as a 64-bit opaque token (base62 URL-safe) to limit header size and make it compiler-friendly
Node: implement using async_hooks with a fast-path no-op when anchor not set; use WeakRef map from token->span handle to avoid leaks
Python: use contextvars for fast path and add optional integration with asyncio.Task.get_name for debuggability
Server: accept x-rw-telemetry-anchor header; if present, translate to inproc anchor token and attach to spawned worker traces
Sampling: do not change sampling decision on anchor attach; include sampling hint flags but respect upstream samplers
Backwards compatibility: preserve b3/traceparent headers; anchor is additive and used only by Redwood SDKs and server runtime
Testing: microbench harness for attach/detach on Node and Python; integration scenarios for WebSocket reconnect and streaming chunk handlers
Observability: add new per-route dashboard panels showing % requests with anchor present and repro ratio for lost-span incidents
risks: Header proliferation causing issues with some proxies - will gate by size and enable explicit opt-in for private deployments
Memory leak risk if WeakRef path not robust across Node versions; will add leak-detection job in CI
Potential subtle interactions with sampling and tail-sampling pipelines; coordinate with sampling owners before rollout
